title: Methodus generalior numeros quosvis satis grandes perscrutandi utrum sint primi necne?

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler tests numbers for primality and factors them using the idoneal number 1848. An idoneal number n has the property that a number with exactly one representation n·x² + y² (with gcd conditions) is prime. A composite number has a second representation, and that second representation yields a factor. Here he takes N = 1848a² + 197² and looks for a second representation N = 1848x² + y². Subtracting the two gives 197² − y² = 1848(x² − a²). Earlier (pp. 44–45) he split the search into four residue cases. At the top of this page he records the parametrisations of those cases:
- case 2: z = ±21s;
- case 3: z = 21s − 9·197 with s = t + 84, so z = ±21t − 9 (check: 21·84 − 1773 = −9);
- case 4: z = 21s + 7·197 with s = t − 66, so z = ±21t − 7 (check: −1386 + 1379 = −7).

§73, a = 1: N = 1848 + 38809 = 40657. Case 1 gives a² + 8 = 9 = x², so x = 3, t = 0, z = −16, y = 155. Indeed 1848·9 + 155² = 16632 + 24025 = 40657. From p/q = (a ± x)/(b ± y) = (1 − 3)/(197 − 155) he gets 1/21 in absolute value. Then 1848·1 + 21² = 2289 = 21·109, so 109 is a factor: 40657 = 109·373.

§74, a = 2: N = 7392 + 38809 = 46201. Case 3 gives a² + 21 = 25 = x², so x = 5, t = 0, z = −9, y = ±1. Indeed 1848·25 + 1 = 46201. Then p/q = (2 + 5)/(197 − 1) = 7/196 = 1/28. Next 1848 + 784 = 2632 = 56·47; dividing by 56 gives 33 + 14 = 47. So 46201 = 47·983.

§75: rather than treat every a, he tabulates the primes 1848a² + 197² for a = 3, 5–8, 13–17, 19, 22–24, 26, 28, 30, 40, 50, 70, 80, 100. The last entry is 18518809.

§76: he calls this an 'inexhaustible source' of primes in the millions. The idea is to vary 197 or use other idoneal numbers. On the next page he reports that no idoneal numbers exist up to 7000.

The page serves the practical goal of certifying and finding large primes, and factoring composites, via the uniqueness of representation by idoneal forms.
errors: Euler writes y = −9·22 + 197 = 1, but the arithmetic gives −1. The sign is immaterial because y enters squared.
In §75 and in the table title the form is printed '1848aa + 197'; it should be 1848aa + 197², as §76 states.
In §73 the reduced fraction 1/21 actually comes from (1 − 3)/(197 − 155) = −1/21 (the other choice gives 1/88). The signs are suppressed but the result is right.

I recomputed all tabulated values from 1848a² + 38809 and they are correct. I verified primality by trial division for 55441 and 85009. The omitted a = 4 value is composite (68377 = 101·677), consistent with the table. I did not check every large entry. The reliance on idoneality is sound given Euler's (and Gauss's) characterisation of the 65 idoneal numbers.

ideas.what: Factoring a number from two distinct representations by an idoneal form n·x² + y², via the fraction (a ± x)/(b ± y) reduced to p/q, followed by gcd/descent with n·p² + q²
ideas.modern_name: Euler's factorization method via two representations by a binary quadratic form (genus theory / idoneal numbers)
ideas.where_published: Euler's memoirs on numeri idonei, e.g. E369, E708, E715, E719, E725 (Nova Acta / Nouveaux Mémoires); I am unsure of every exact E-number.

ideas.what: Generating large primes as 1848a² + 197² using the largest idoneal number 1848, with the explicit prime 18518809
ideas.modern_name: Primality certification via idoneal forms (Euler's convenient numbers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (the 18518809 example, letter to Béguelin c. 1778)
ideas.where_published: Euler's letter to Béguelin in Nouveaux Mémoires de l'Académie de Berlin (c. 1776/78); also E719 itself; discussed in Dickson, History vol. I, and Weil.

ideas.what: Residue-case parametrisations of z to speed up the search for a second representation
ideas.modern_name: Sieving / exclusion by residues in the search for representations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler; later the Gauss exclusion method
ideas.where_published: E719 (this memoir) and related idoneal-number memoirs

deep.surprise_reason: These are worked examples of Euler's well-documented idoneal-number primality and factoring method, and the 18518809 example is famous. The arithmetic is correct and there is nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'y = −9·22 + 197 = 1' evaluates to −1; Euler's printed sign is immaterial.
The table heading and §75 read '1848aa + 197' in print; the intended form is 1848aa + 197² (as in §76).
'fiat p/q = (a+x)/(b−y) [?] = 1/28' is consistent: (2+5)/(197−1) = 7/196 = 1/28. The [?] can be removed.
The page numbers are 46–47 (Nova Acta XIV), not those of the previous-page transcription.
